problem: H is defined only as 'a vector space with an inner product'. The standard definition of a Hilbert space also requires completeness (it is a complete inner-product space), and an examiner will expect that word.
fix: H is a complete complex vector space with an inner product (a Hilbert space). For finite-dimensional qubit systems every inner-product space is complete, so the two definitions coincide here.

problem: U(t)=e^{-iHt/ħ} is written without saying it holds only when the Hamiltonian H does not depend on time. With a time-dependent H the exponent becomes an integral and students who copy this blindly lose marks.
fix: Add: this closed form holds for a time-independent Hamiltonian; if H depends on time, U(t) is the time-ordered exponential of -iHt/ħ.

problem: The sentence 'Amplitudes are not probabilities; their modulus squared are' has broken grammar and can be misread as saying the amplitudes themselves are squares.
fix: Write: 'Amplitudes are not probabilities; the probability of each outcome is the modulus squared of its amplitude.'

problem: 'A projective measurement uses Hermitian operators' can be misread as saying the measurement itself is an operator; the operato is the observable being measured.
fix: Write: 'A projective measurement is described by a Hermitian operator, the observable A.'
